reasoning_traces.think:
The primitives represent fundamental probabilistic structures underlying NFL fantasy operations. The draft pick distribution uses a multinomial model with uniform probabilities, assuming equal opportunity across teams. League size follows a multiplicative power-law influenced by participation, time, fees, and competition. Pick value incorporates expected returns minus risk-adjusted volatility, reflecting rational player behavior. Team scoring adheres to a gamma distribution, capturing positive skewness in point totals. These operators are dualized through GSI and GSE mappings: fantasy utilities become valuation metrics, league dynamics inform scarcity pricing, pick value guides strategic allocation, and scoring distributions parameterize state transitions. Failure occurs when independence assumptions break, leading to skewed drafts, divergent leagues, irrational picks, or heavy-tailed scoring. Veto conditions include multicollinearity among factors and leakage of information across layers.
